# ![GBrain](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/raw/v0.60.757.0/docs/images/brand/gbrain-wordmark.svg)

**One brain for you and your company, read by every agent you use.** Put your own notes and your company's docs in one place: a facts page, a decisions log, call transcripts. Claude Code, Codex and your other agents look there before they answer, so they stop starting from zero and work from what you and your team actually wrote down.

GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host, and it starts with no API keys: search is by keyword until you add one. gbrain.io is optional paid hosting.

Tip

**Need hosted? First time running an agent?** Try **[gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=readme)**, hosted GBrain, for the easiest experience: one brain for you and your team, connected to ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor, with nothing to install or keep online. Stuck? Email [support@gbrain.io](mailto:support@gbrain.io) and a person will set it up with you, free.

**A few minutes after you install it:**

- Every new Claude Code or Codex session looks in your brain before it answers, without being told to.
- Anything you ask your agent to remember is still there in the next session, in every agent connected to the brain.
- Your notes and your company's docs are searchable, and your agent answers questions like *"what did we decide about pricing, and why?"* from them.

## Stability

New releases come out many times a day, but the install command below gives you the **stable channel**: a release reaches it only after the full test suite and a two-hour, 600,000-page load test pass on that exact release, and only when an important fix is waiting or stable is a week old. Updates are never installed without your say-so unless you turn on automatic upgrades. After an upgrade, gbrain shows a one-time notice listing what changed in behaviour. Stable also comes with a written promise about which commands, flags, tools, config keys and output fields stay the same, and how much warning you get before one changes. [docs/STABILITY.md](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/v0.60.757.0/docs/STABILITY.md) explains that promise, how often stable moves, how to pin a version or go back, and what the faster alpha channel is for.

gbrain v0.60.757.0 is installed at /harness-state/.local/bin/gbrain, and `gbrain --version` prints `gbrain 0.60.757.0`.

I didn't use the `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.757.0` command the docs give. Hermes blocked the Bun installer because it pipes a download straight into a shell, and nobody was here to approve it. Instead I used the docs' Hermes route: the single prebuilt file from the release, downloaded from the v0.60.757.0 tag rather than "latest", so the version is pinned.

Setup:
- `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` created a local brain that needs no API keys. Search is keyword-only until you add an embedding key.
- `gbrain setup hermes` registered the gbrain tool server with Hermes, and `hermes mcp test gbrain` connects.
- Setup also added the "check gbrain first" instructions to /harness-state/hermes/SOUL.md and a hook that runs before each reply in /harness-state/hermes/config.yaml.
- Setup printed an error saying that hook wasn't active, but `hermes hooks doctor` shows it allowlisted and healthy, so the warning looks wrong.
- A save-and-recall test worked. I deleted the test fact afterwards.

Start a new Hermes session to load gbrain. /harness-state/.local/bin isn't on PATH in this shell, so use the full path or add it to PATH.

To install the same version with Bun instead, allow risky commands in single-query mode (`approvals.single_query_mode: approve` in config.yaml) or run the command yourself.
